Ordnance 0.4.7. The in-game menu has two panes and takes the mouse. Mods that bring their own boot script run, including Objective Tracker.

## What's new

**In-game menu.** F10 opens it. Mods are on the left, and the selected mod's settings are on the right. The mouse works. A long list of options starts folded. Esc or right-click goes back to the mod list. The menu sits clear of the game's own HUD. Arrow keys still move one row. Right arrow rebinds a key. Enter stays the chat key.

**Boot-script mods run.** Some mods replace the game's boot script instead of declaring an addon. Objective Tracker is one. Ordnance stays the boot and starts that script. You do not install another loader.

**Updating from the browser finishes.** Installing a newer copy of a mod you already have no longer sits on the handoff window. The mod updates in place, then redeploys if it is enabled.

**Library.** Categories and profiles have a color. The library can be searched and sorted. Dragging a mod in the profile list shows a line where it will land. Add to top and Add to bottom are in the row menu. Lower in the list wins when two mods change the same file.

**New icon.**

Sign in to Nexus Mods still says Coming soon. An API key in Settings is how update checks reach Nexus until Nexus issues a client id.

## What Ordnance does

**Import from your current mod manager.** One-click import from HD2 Arsenal and Echelon — plus the older HD2 mod manager, Vortex, and your Downloads folder, with names, on/off state, and options intact.

**Automatic update checking and (optionally) downloading.** Ordnance checks every mod against its source — AyakaMods, GitHub, GameBanana, ModWorkshop, and Nexus Mods — and, when you enable it, downloads and installs the ones it can fetch itself.

**One deploy, everything enabled.** Merge mods and generated stat-plan edits into a single sealed swap and a single boot script. No per-mod loader conflicts.

## Get it

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `Ordnance-0.4.7-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.7-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | `Ordnance-0.4.7-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux (Fedora/openSUSE) | `Ordnance-0.4.7-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: no install | `Ordnance-0.4.7-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `Ordnance-0.4.7-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

**Browser extension:** `ordnance-extension-chrome-1.0.4.zip` or `ordnance-extension-firefox-1.0.4.zip`. Load it unpacked. On a Nexus Files tab, the button beside Manual download says Ordnance.

Found a problem? Open an issue: <https://github.com/Cavadus/ordnance/issues>
